itemratio.title: itemratio.txt
itemratio.overview:
This file determines the quality of items when being spawned. After the game determines what Item Type should spawn, it then uses this file to calculate the quality of that item. These Item Quality checks are used for most item drops in the game such as monster drops and chest drops.
For a writeup on how these fields are used, see Item Ratio Calculations.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Version
fields.description: Defines which game version to use this item ratio (0 = Classic mode | 100 = Expansion mode)

fields.name: Uber
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item ratio will apply to items with Exceptional or Elite Quality. If equals 0, then the item ratio will apply to Normal Quality items (This is determined by the normcode (armor), ubercode (armor), and ultracode (armor) fields in weapons.txt / armor.txt)

fields.name: Class Specific
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item ratio will apply to class-based items (This will compare to the Class (itemtypes) field to determine if the item is class specific)

fields.name: Rarity
fields.description: Base value for calculating the specific Quality chance. Higher value means rarer chance. (Calculation order is Unique -> Set -> Rare -> Magic -> HiQuality -> Normal)

fields.name: Divisor
fields.description: Modifier for changing the specific Quality chance, based on the difference between the Monster Level and the Item's base level

fields.name: Min
fields.description: The minimum value of the probability denominator for specific Quality. This is compared to the calculated specific Quality value after Magic Find calculations and is chosen if it is greater than that value. (Calculated in 128ths)

itemstatcost.title: ItemStatCost.txt
itemstatcost.overview:
This file controls the functionalities for each possible stat on a unit. These defined stats are used to form modifiers for the properties.txt and PropertyGroups.txt files.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Stat
fields.description: Defines the unique pointer for this stat, which is used in other files

fields.name: Send Other
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then only add the stat to a new monster if the that has no state and has an item mask. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Signed
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the stat will be treated as a signed integer, meaning that it can be either a positive or negative value. If equals 0, then stat will be treated as an unsigned integer, meaning that it can only be a positive value. This only affects stats with state bits.

fields.name: Send Bits
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data for the stat to send to the game client, essentially controlling the max value possible for the stat. Signed values should have less than 32 bits, otherwise they will be treated as unsigned values.

fields.name: Send Param Bits
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data for the stat's parameter value to send to the client for a unit. This value is always treated as a signed integer.

fields.name: UpdateAnimRate
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the stat will notify that game to handle and adjust the speed of the unit when the stat changes. If equals 0, then ignore this. This is only checked for stats with states or for specific skill server functions including 30, 61, 71.

fields.name: Saved
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this state will be inserted in the change list to be stored in the Character Save file. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: CSvSigned
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the stat will be saved as a signed integer in the Character Save file. If equals 0, then the stat will be saved as an unsigned integer in the Character Save file. This is only used if the Saved field is enabled.

fields.name: CSvBits
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data for the stat to send to save in the Character Save file. Signed values should have less than 32 bits, otherwise they will be treated as unsigned values. This is only used if the Saved field is enabled.

fields.name: CSvParam
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data for the stat's parameter value to save in the Character Save file. This value is always treated as a signed integer. This is only used if the Saved field is enabled.

fields.name: fCallback
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then any changes to the stat will call the Callback function which will update the character's states, skills, or item events based on the changed stat value. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: fMin
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the stat will have a minimum value that cannot be reduced further than that value (See MinAccr field). If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: MinAccr
fields.description: The minimum value of a stat. This is only used if the fMin field is enabled.

fields.name: Encode
fields.description: Controls how the stat will modify an item's buy, sell, and repair costs. This field uses a code value to select a function to handle the calculations. This field relies on the Add, Multiply and ValShift fields. The baseline Stat Value is first modified using the ValShift field to shift the bits. This Stat Value is then used in the calculations by one of the selected functions.
table:
Buy Cost += [Stat Value] * [Multiply] / 1024 + [Add]
Sell Cost += [Stat Value] * [Multiply] / 1024 + [Add]
Repair Cost += [Stat Value] * [Multiply] / 1024 + [Add]

Use the stat's parameter value to determine the skill ID used. Use the stat's value to determine the skill level. Obtain the cost mult (skills) and cost add (skills) values from the skill linked in this stat's parameter. The Stat Value is considered the skill's level.
Buy Cost += [Stat Value] * [cost mult (skills)] / 1024 + [cost add (skills)]
Sell Cost += [Stat Value] * [cost mult (skills)] / 4096 + [cost add (skills)]
Repair Cost += [Stat Value] * [cost mult (skills)] / 1024 + [cost add (skills)]

Use the stat's parameter value to determine both the skill ID and skill level. Obtain the cost mult (skills) and cost add (skills) values from the determined skill ID.
Buy Cost += [Stat Value] * [cost mult (skills)] / 1024 + [cost add (skills)]
Sell Cost += [Stat Value] * [cost mult (skills)] / 4096 + [cost add (skills)]
Repair Cost += [Stat Value] * [cost mult (skills)] / 1024 + [cost add (skills)]

Obtains the stat's min and max values based on the By Time bit masks and uses them to calculate the average value or Baseline stat value.
Buy Cost += [Baseline] * [Multiply] / 1024 + [Add]
Sell Cost += [Baseline] * [Multiply] / 1024 + [Add]
Repair Cost += [Baseline] * [Multiply] / 1024 + [Add]

fields.name: Add
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the Encode function. Flat integer modification to the Unique item's buy, sell, and repair costs. This is added after the Multiply field has modified the costs.

fields.name: Multiply
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the Encode function. Multiplicative modifier for the item's buy, sell, and repair costs. The way this value is used depends on the Encode function selected.

fields.name: ValShift
fields.description: Used to shift the stat's input value by a number of bits to obtain the actual value when performing calculations (such as for the Encode function).

fields.name: 1.09-Save Bits
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data are allocated for the overall size of the stat when saving/reading an item from a Character Save. This value can be treated as a signed or unsigned integer, depending on the stat. This field is only used for items saved in a game version of Patch 1.09d or older.

fields.name: 1.09-Save Add
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data are allocated for the stat's value when saving/reading an item from a Character Save. This value is treated as a signed integer. This field is only used for items saved in a game version of Patch 1.09d or older.

fields.name: Save Bits
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data are allocated for the overall size of the stat when saving/reading an item from a Character Save. This value can be treated as a signed or unsigned integer, depending on the stat.

fields.name: Save Add
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data are allocated for the stat's value when saving/reading an item from a Character Save. This value is treated as a signed integer.

fields.name: Save Param Bits
fields.description: Controls how many bits of data for the stat's parameter value to use when saving/reading an item from a Character Save. This value is always treated as an unsigned integer.

fields.name: keepzero
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this stat will remain on the stat change list, when being updated, even if that stat value is 0. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: op
fields.description: This is the stat operator, used for advanced stat modification when calculating the value of a stat. This can involves using this stat and its value to modify another stat's value. This use a function ID to determine what to calculate.
table: No operator. Just add the stat normally

Percent Operator. Gets the value of op stat# and multiplies it by a percentage increase equal to this stat's value:
[op stat#] += [op stat#] * value / 100

op param
op base
op stat#

By Level Operator. Gets value of op stat# and uses it as a multiplier with op param as the divisor:
[op stat#] += [op stat#] * [op base] << [op param]

op param
op base
op stat#

By Level Percent Operator. Gets value of op stat# and uses it as a multiplier with op param as the divisor. Then it uses this value as a percentage increase to op stat#:
percent = [op stat#] * [op base] << [op param]
[op stat#] = [op stat#] * percent / 100

op param
op base
op stat#

By Level Source Operator. Gets value of op stat# for the item (not the unit) and uses it as a multiplier with op param as the divisor:
[op stat#] += [op stat#] * [op base] << [op param]

op param
op base
op stat#

By Level Source Percent Operator. Gets value of op stat# for the item (not the unit) and uses it as a multiplier with op param as the divisor. Then it uses this value as a percentage increase to op stat#:
percent = [op stat#] * [op base] << [op param]
[op stat#] = [op stat#] * percent / 100

By Time Operator. Gets the value of op stat# and increases it by a delta value which depends on game's time of day. The delta is calculated by using the stat's min and max as a range of increase/decrease and biasing this value with the current progress of game's time of day
[op stat#] += [op stat#] * [delta]

By Time Percent Operator. Gets the value of op stat# and multiplies it by a percentage. This percentage is determined by obtaining op stat# and a delta value which depends on game's time of day. The delta is calculated by using the stat's min and max as a range of increase/decrease and biasing this value with the current progress of game's time of day
percent = [op stat#] * [delta]
[op stat#] = [op stat#] * percent / 100

Energy Operator. This will only apply for stats on the player. Gets the value of op stat# and multiplies it by the related ManaPerMagic (charstats) field. This is then bit shifted by the baseline Mana bit value, MANA_SHIFT = 8, with the fourths value calculation from the ManaPerMagic (charstats) field.
[op stat#] = [op stat#] * [ManaPerMagic (charstats)] << (MANA_SHIFT - 2)

Vitality Operator. This will only apply for stats on the player.
If the stat is "maxstamina", then the operator will get the value of op stat# and multiply it by the related StaminaPerVitality (charstats) field. This is then bit shifted by the baseline Stamina bit value, STAMINA_SHIFT = 8, with the fourths value calculation from the StaminaPerVitality (charstats) field:
[op stat#] = [op stat#] * [StaminaPerVitality (charstats)] << (STAMINA_SHIFT - 2)
If the stat is not "maxstamina", then the operator will get the value of op stat# and multiply it by the related LifePerVitality (charstats) field. This is then bit shifted by the baseline Life bit value, LIFE_SHIFT = 8, with the fourths value calculation from the LifePerVitality (charstats) field:
[op stat#] = [op stat#] * [LifePerVitality (charstats)] << (LIFE_SHIFT - 2)
Currently not being used. Does nothing.

Player Percent Operator. This will only apply for stats on units. Gets the value of op stat# and multiplies it by a percentage increase equal to this stat's value:
[op stat#] += [op stat#] * value / 100

Item Percent Operator. This will only apply for stats on items. Gets the value of op stat# and multiplies it by a percentage increase equal to this stat's value:
[op stat#] += [op stat#] * value / 100

fields.name: op param
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the op function.

fields.name: op base
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the op function.

fields.name: op stat#
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the op function.

fields.name: direct
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then when the stat is being updated in certain skill functions having to do with state changes, the stat will update in relation to its maxstat field to ensure that it never exceeds that value. If equals 0, then ignore this, and the stat will simply update in these cases. This only applies to skills that use skill server function 65, 66, 81, and 82.

fields.name: maxstat
fields.description: Controls which stat is associated with this stat to be treated as the maximum version of this stat. This means that 2 stats are essentially linked so that there can be a current version of the stat and a maximum version to control the cap of stat's value. This is used for Life, Mana, Stamina, and Durability. This field relies on the direct field to be enabled unless it is being used for the healing potion item spell.

fields.name: damagerelated
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this stat will be exclusive to the item and will not add to the unit. If equals 0, then ignore this, and the stat will always add to the unit. This is typically used for weapons and is important when dual wielding weapons so that when a unit attacks, then one weapon's stats do not stack with another weapon's stats.

fields.name: itemevent#
fields.description: Uses an event that will activate the specified function defined by itemeventfunc#. This points to the ID of an event defined in the events.txt file.

fields.name: itemeventfunc#
fields.description: Specifies the functiion to use after the related item event occurred. Functions are defined by a numeric ID code and correspond to Server Event Functions (enums). This is only applied based on the itemevent# field definition.

fields.name: descpriority
fields.description: Controls how this stat is sorted in item tooltips. This field is compared to the same field on other stats to determine how to order the stats. The higher the value means that the stat will be sorted higher than other stats. If more than 1 stat has the same descpriority value, then they will be listed in the order defined in this data file.

fields.name: descfunc
fields.description: Controls how the stat is displayed in tooltips. Uses an ID value to select a description function to format the string value.
table:
Plus or Minus
If value > 0, "+[value] [descstr]"
If value < 0, "-[value] [descstr]"

Plus or Minus Per Level
If value > 0, "+[value] [descstr] [descstr2]"
If value < 0, "-[value] [descstr] [descstr2]"

Repair
Uses the string "ModStre9t" and inserts the value into this string

Plus Sub One
If value > 1, then use "+[value] [descstr]"
Else, use "[value] [descstr]" or "-[value] [descstr]"

Add Class Skill
Uses the StrAllSkills (charstats)

Add Tab Skill
Uses StrSkillTab# (charstats) based on related tab being modified

Proc Skill
Gets the skill name, skill level, and chance percent to insert into the descstrpos string

Aura
Gets the skill name, and uses the stat's value for the skill level and inserts these values into the designated "descstr" string

Plus Minus By Time
Gets the proper value based on the time of day and inserts this value into the "descstr" string
Uses the following strings for the second part of the description, depending on the time selected: "ModStre9d", "ModStre9e", "ModStre9f", "ModStre9g"

Sprintf Num
Uses the Sprintf string function with the designated "descstr" string and adds descstr2 if that value is not empty

Minus Percent Per Level
"[value * -1]% [descstr] [descstr2]"
If descstr2 is empty, then default to using the "increaseswithplaylevelX" string

Versus Monster Percent
Uses strplur (montype) based on the monster type selected, and inserts this value into the designated "descstr" string

Reanimate
Obtains the related NameStr (monstats) string and inserts this string into the designated "descstr" string

Charges
Obtains the skill, skill level, max charges, and current charges and inserts these values into the designated "descstr" string

Minus
If desval equals 1, then use "+[value * -1] [descstr]"
If desval equals 2, then use "[descstr] +[value * -1]"

Single Skill
Obtains the str name (skilldesc) and the StrClassOnly (charstats)
Uses the stat value as the skill level
Combines these values into the designated "descstr" string

Non Class Skill
Obtains the str name (skilldesc)
Uses the stat value as the skill level
Combines these values into the designated "descstr" string

Sprintf num positive
Same as function 19, except the it uses the absolute value of [value]

fields.name: descval
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the descfunc function. This controls the how the value of the stat is displayed.
table: Do not show the value of the stat
Shows the value of the stat at the start of its description
Shows the value of the stat at the end of its description

fields.name: descstrpos
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the descfunc function. This uses a string to display the item stat in a tooltip when its value is positive.

fields.name: descstrneg
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the descfunc function. This uses a string to display the item stat in a tooltip when its value is negative.

fields.name: descstr2
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the descfunc function. This uses a string to append to an item stat's string in a tooltip.

fields.name: dgrp
fields.description: Assigns the stat to a group ID value. If all stats with a matching dgrp value are applied on the unit, then instead of displaying each stat individually, the group description will be applied instead (see dgrpfunc field)

fields.name: dgrpfunc
fields.description: Controls how the shared group of stats is displayed in tooltips. Uses an ID value to select a description function to format the string value. This function IDs are exactly the same as the descfunc field, see that description for more details.

fields.name: dgrpval
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the dgrpfunc function. This controls the how the value of the stat is displayed. (Functions the same as the descval field)

fields.name: dgrpstrpos
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the dgrpfunc function. This uses a string to display the item stat in a tooltip when its value is positive.

fields.name: dgrpstrneg
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the dgrpfunc function. This uses a string to display the item stat in a tooltip when its value is negative.

fields.name: dgrpstr2
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter value for the dgrpfunc function. This uses a string to append to an item stat's string in a tooltip.

fields.name: stuff
fields.description: Used as a bit shift value for handling the conversion of skill IDs and skill levels to bit values for the stat. Controls the numeric range of possible skill IDs and skill levels for charge based items. This value cannot be less than or equal to 0, or greater than 8, otherwise it will default to 6. The row that this value appears in the data file is unrelated, since this is a universally applied value.

fields.name: advdisplay
fields.description: Controls how the stat appears in the Advanced Stats UI
table: The stat will never appear on the Advanced Stats UI
The stat will always show on the Advanced Stats UI
The stat will only show on the Advanced Stats UI if the value is greater than 0

itemtypes.title: ItemTypes.txt
itemtypes.overview:
This file controls the general statistics for each type of item, which is then used for the item type fields in other files.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Code
fields.description: Defines the unique pointer for this Item Type, which is used by other data files

fields.name: Equiv#
fields.description: Points to the index of another Item Type to reference as a parent. This is used to create a hierarchy for Item Types where the parents will have more universal settings shared across the related children

fields.name: Repair
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item can be repaired by an NPC in the shop UI. If equals 0, then the item cannot be repaired.

fields.name: Body
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item can be equipped by a character (also will require the BodyLoc# fields as parameters). If equals 0, then the item can only be carried in the inventory, stash, or Horadric Cube.

fields.name: BodyLoc#
fields.description: These are required parameters if the Body field is enabled. These fields specify the inventory slots where the item can be equipped.

fields.name: Shoots
fields.description: Points to the index of another Item Type as the required equipped Item Type to be used as ammo

fields.name: Quiver
fields.description: Points to the index of another Item Type as the required equipped Item Type to be used as this ammos weapon

fields.name: Throwable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then it determines that this item is a throwing weapon. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Reload
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item (considered ammo in this case) will be automatically transferred from the inventory to the required BodyLoc# when another item runs out of that specific ammo. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: ReEquip
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item in the inventory will replace a matching equipped item if that equipped item was destroyed. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: AutoStack
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then if the player picks up a matching Item Type, then they will try to automatically stack together. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Magic
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item will always have the Magic quality (unless it is a Quest item). If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Rare
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item can spawn as a Rare quality. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Normal
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item will always have the Normal quality. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Beltable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item can be placed in the character's belt slots. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: MaxSockets#
fields.description: Determines the maximum possible number of sockets that can be spawned on the item when the item level is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to the MaxSocketsLevelThreshold# value. The number of sockets is capped by the gemsockets (armor), gemsockets (weapons), gemsockets (misc) value.

fields.name: MaxSocketsLevelThreshold#
fields.description: Defines the item level threshold between successive MaxSockets# fields. Ex: If MaxSocketsLevelThreshold1 is met, use MaxSockets2. If MaxSocketsLevelThreshold2 is met, use MaxSockets3.

fields.name: TreasureClass
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then allow this Item Type to be used in default treasure classes. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Rarity
fields.description: Determines the chance for the item to spawn with stats, when created as a random Weapon/Armor/Misc item. Used in the following formula: IF RANDOM(0, ([Rarity] - [Current Act Level])) > 0, THEN spawn stats

fields.name: StaffMods
fields.description: Determines if the Item Type should have class specific item skill modifiers

fields.name: Class
fields.description: Determines if this item should be useable only by a specific class

fields.name: VarInvGfx
fields.description: Tracks the number of inventory graphics used for this item type. This number much match the number of InvGfx# fields used.

fields.name: InvGfx#
fields.description: Defines a DC6 file to use for the item's inventory graphics. The amount of this fields used should match the value used in VarInvGfx

fields.name: StorePage
fields.description: Uses a code to determine which UI tab page on the NPC shop UI to display this Item Type, such as after it is sold to the NPC.

fields.name: UICategory
fields.description: Determines what UI Category this item type will be displayed in (used for loot filter and chronicle uniques page). All items that have this type as their type1 will display in the loot filter under this category, unless the item overrides it in misc/armor/weapon files

fields.name: RunewordCategory#
fields.description: Determines what Runeword UI Category this item type will be displayed in (used the chronicle runewords page). Different item types have different runeword UI categories assigned to them. This is then used in the Chronicle runewords page, where it checks each runeword's itype# (runes), and then the associated RunewordCategory# for each valid itype to decide which runewords should be filtered on each category

fields.name: Restricted
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, this item type is now restricted. Only one item of a given restricted type may be present across all equipped + socketed items. Multiple different restricted types are allowed.

itemuicategories.title: ItemUICategories.txt
itemuicategories.overview: This file defines the item categories that are used in the loot filter and also the chronicle's unique page. ItemTypes.txt assigns its types to the corresponding categories, and item themselves in armor/weapon/misc files can also override their UI category

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The name acts as an ID for the category, its index correlates to the ItemUICategory enum. This name will be saved into the shareable loot filter profile jsons when a category is filtered. It is also used as a key in the string table to display localized names in game.

fields.name: isEquipment
fields.description: Boolean field. If 1, this category is put into the 'equipment' panel. If 0, this category is put in the 'misc' panel

fields.name: ParentCategory
fields.description: The parent category of this category. Must match a previous entry's name. Null means this is a top-level category. NOTE: We only support a single level of parent-child relationship. A parent category cannot have a parent, its parent must be null

fields.name: QualityFilter
fields.description: Boolean field. If 1, the quality filter will apply to this category. If 0, the quality filter will not apply. Currently only applies to Equipment categories, misc categories will ignore this field

fields.name: NumColumns
fields.description: Define how many columns a category should display in. Min = 1, Max = 3. Ignored if category uses the quality filter, since we change the number of columns based on the qualities selected

levelgroups.title: LevelGroups.txt
levelgroups.overview: This file controls how the game groups levels together. This is mainly used for condensing level names in desecrated (terror) zone messaging

fields.name: LevelGroupId
fields.description: Defines the unique name pointer for the level group, which is used in other files

fields.name: ParentLevelGroupId
fields.description: Defines a parent for this level group. If the parent group is completed then this level group will not be displayed.

fields.name: CompleteThreshold
fields.description: Percent amount of the level group to satisfy before it is marked as completed.

fields.name: Effect
fields.description: Controls what effect to play for this level group when it is completed.
table: Play a random cow attack, hit, or death sound

fields.name: NameString
fields.description: String Field. Used for displaying the name of the level group, such as when all levels in a group have been desecrated.

levels.title: Levels.txt
levels.overview: This file controls how the game controls the area levels, including how the level is built, what rules are allowed on the level, and what monsters/objects can spawn on the level.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Defines the unique name pointer for the area level, which is used in other files

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Defines the unique numeric ID for the area level, which is used in other files

fields.name: Pal
fields.description: Defines which palette file to use for the area level. This uses index values from 0 to 4 to convey Act 1 to Act 5.

fields.name: Act
fields.description: Defines the Act number that the area level is a part of. This uses index values from 0 to 4 to convey Act 1 to Act 5.

fields.name: QuestFlag
fields.description: Controls what quest record that the player needs to have completed before being allowed to enter this area level, while playing in Classic Mode. Each quest can have multiple quest records, and this field is looking for a specific quest record from a quest.

fields.name: QuestFlagEx
fields.description: Controls what quest record that the player needs to have completed before being allowed to enter this area level, while playing in Expansion Mode. Each quest can have multiple quest records, and this field is looking for a specific quest record from a quest.

fields.name: Layer
fields.description: Defines a unique numeric ID that is used to identify which Automap data belongs to which area level when saving and loading data from the character save.

fields.name: SizeX
fields.description: Specifies the Length tile size values of an entire area level, which are used for determining how to build the level, for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively.

fields.name: SizeY
fields.description: Specifies the Width tile size values of an entire area level, which are used for determining how to build the level, for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively.

fields.name: OffsetX
fields.description: Specifies the location X offset coordinate (measured in tile size) for the origin point of the area level in the world.

fields.name: OffsetY
fields.description: Specifies the location offset Y coordinate (measured in tile size) for the origin point of the area level in the world.

fields.name: CompletionTotalRoomsOverride
fields.description: If > 0, use this value as the total number of rooms in the level for calculating its level completion percentage. Otherwise, use the total amount of populateable rooms.

fields.name: Depend
fields.description: Assigns another level to be this area level's depended level, which controls this area level's position and how it starts building its tiles. Uses the Id field. If this equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Teleport
fields.description: Controls the functionality of teleport skills like Sorceress Teleport and Assassin Dragon Flight on the area level
table: Teleport is disabled on the area level
Teleport is enabled on the area level
Teleport is enabled on the area level but adheres to the collision of the rooms

fields.name: Rain
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then allow rain to play its effects on the area level. If the level is part of Act 5, then it will snow on the area level, instead of rain. If equals 0, then it will never rain on the area level.

fields.name: Mud
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then random bubbles will animate on the tiles that are flagged as water tiles. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: NoPer
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then allow the use of display option of Perspective Mode while the player is in the level. If equals 0, then disable the option of Perspective Mode and force the player to use Orthographic Mode while the player is in the level.

fields.name: LOSDraw
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then the level will check the player's line of sight before drawing monsters. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: FloorFilter
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1 and if the floor's layer in the area level equals 1, then draw the floor tiles with a linear texture sampler. If equals 0, then draw the floor tiles with a nearest texture sampler.

fields.name: BlankScreen
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then draw the area level screen. If equals 0, then do not draw the area level screen, meaning that the level will be a blank screen.

fields.name: DrawEdges
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then draw the areas in levels that are not covered by floor tiles. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: DrlgType
fields.description: Determines the type of Dynamic Random Level Generation used for building and handling different elements of the area level. Uses a numeric code to handle which type of DRLG is used.

fields.name: LevelType
fields.description: Defines the Level Type used for this area level. Uses Id (lvltypes), which is determined by what order it is defined in the lvltypes.txt file.

fields.name: SubType
fields.description: Controls the group of tile substitutions for the area level (see lvlsub.txt). There are defined sub types to choose from.

fields.name: SubTheme
fields.description: Controls which theme number to use in a Level Substitution (See lvlsub.txt). The allowed values are 0 to 4, which convey which Prob# (lvlsub), Trials# (lvlsub), and Max# (lvlsub) field to use. If this equals -1, then there is no sub theme for the area level.

fields.name: SubWaypoint
fields.description: Controls the level substitutions for adding waypoints in the area level (see lvlsub.txt). This uses a defined sub type to choose from (See SubType). This will depend on the room having a waypoint tile.

fields.name: SubShrine
fields.description: Controls the level substitutions for adding shrines in the area level (see lvlsub.txt). This uses a defined sub type to choose from (See SubType). This will depend on the room allowing for a shrine to spawn.

fields.name: Vis#
fields.description: Defines the visibility of other area levels involved with this area level, allowing for travel functionalities between levels. This uses the Id field of another defined area level to link with this area level. If this equals 0, then no area level is specified.

fields.name: Warp#
fields.description: Uses the Id (lvlwarp) field, which defines which Level Warp to use when exiting the area level. This is connected with the definition of the related Vis# field. If this equals -1, then no Level Warp is specified which should also mean that the related Vis# field is not defined.

fields.name: Intensity
fields.description: Controls the intensity value of the area level's ambient colors. This affects brightness of the room's RGB colors. Uses a value between 0 and 128. If all these related fields equal 0, then the game ignores setting the area level's ambient colors.

fields.name: Red
fields.description: Controls the red value of the area level's ambient colors. Uses a value between 0 and 255.

fields.name: Green
fields.description: Controls the green value of the area level's ambient colors. Uses a value between 0 and 255.

fields.name: Blue
fields.description: Controls the blue value of the area level's ambient colors. Uses a value between 0 and 255.

fields.name: Portal
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this area level will be flagged as a portal level, which is saved in the player's information and can be used for keeping track of the player's portal functionalities. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Position
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then enable special casing for positioning the player on the area level. This can mean that the player could spawn on a different location on the area level, depending on the level room's position type. An example can be when the player spawns in a town when loading the game, or using a waypoint, or using a town portal. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: SaveMonsters
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the game will save the monsters in the area level, such as when all players leave the area level. If equals 0, then monsters will not be saved and will be removed. This is usually disabled for areas where monsters do not spawn.

fields.name: Quest
fields.description: Controls what quest record is attached to monsters that spawn in this area level. This is used for specific quests handling lists of monsters in the area level.

fields.name: WarpDist
fields.description: Defines the minimum pixel distance from a Level Warp that a monster is allowed to spawn near. Tile distance values are converted to game pixel distance values by multiplying the tile distance value by 160 / 32, where 160 is the width of pixels of a tile.

fields.name: monlvl
fields.description: Controls the overall monster level for the area level for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively. This is for Classic mode only. This can affect the highest item level allowed to drop in this area level.

fields.name: MonLvlEx
fields.description: Controls the overall monster level for the area level for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively. This is for Expansion mode only. This can affect the highest item level allowed to drop in this area level.

fields.name: MonDen
fields.description: Controls the monster density on the area level for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively. This is a random value out of 100000, which will determine whether to spawn or not spawn a monster pack in the room of the area level. If this value equals 0, then no random monsters will populate on the area level.

fields.name: MonUMin
fields.description: Defines the minimum number of Unique Monsters that can spawn in the area level for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively. This field depends on the related MonDen field being defined.

fields.name: MonUMax
fields.description: Defines the maximum number of Unique Monsters that can spawn in the area level for Normal, Nightmare, and Hell Difficulty, respectively. This field depends on the related MonDen field being defined. Each room in the area level will attempt to spawn a Unique Monster with a 5/100 random chance, and this field's value will cap the number of successful attempts for the entire area level.

fields.name: MonWndr
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then allow Wandering Monsters to spawn on this area level (see wanderingmon.txt). This field depends on the related MonDen field being defined. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: MonSpcWalk
fields.description: Defines a distance value, used to handle monster pathing AI when the level has certain pathing blockers, such as jail bars or rivers. In these cases, monsters will walk randomly until a player is located within this distance value or when the monsters find a possible path to target the player. If this equals 0, then ignore this field.

fields.name: NumMon
fields.description: Controls the number of different monsters randomly spawn in the area level. The maximum value is 13. This controls the number of random selections from the 25 related mon# and umon# fields or nmon# fields, depending on the game difficulty.

fields.name: mon#
fields.description: Defines which monsters can spawn on the area level for Normal Difficulty.

fields.name: rangedspawn
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then for the first monster, try to pick a ranged type. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: nmon#
fields.description: Defines which monsters can spawn on the area level for Nightmare Difficulty and Hell Difficulty.

fields.name: umon#
fields.description: Defines which monsters can spawn as Unique monsters on this area level for Normal Difficulty.

fields.name: cmon#
fields.description: Defines which Critter monsters can spawn on the area level. Critter monsters are determined by the critter (monstats2) field.

fields.name: cpct#
fields.description: Controls the percent chance (out of 100) to spawn a Critter monster on the area level.

fields.name: camt#
fields.description: Controls the amount of Critter monsters to spawn on the area level after they succeeded their random spawn chance from the related cpct# field.

fields.name: Themes
fields.description: Controls the type of theme when building a level room. This value is a summation of possible values to build a bit mask for determining which themes to use when building a level room. For example, a value of 60 means that the area level can have the following themes: 32, 16, 8, 4.

fields.name: SoundEnv
fields.description: Uses the index of an entry from soundenviron.txt, which controls what music is played while the player is in the area level

fields.name: Waypoint
fields.description: Defines the unique numeric ID for the Waypoint in the area level. If this value is greater than or equal to 255, then ignore this field.

fields.name: LevelName
fields.description: String Field. Used for displaying the name of the area level, such as when in the UI when the Automap is being viewed.

fields.name: LevelWarp
fields.description: String Field. Used displaying the entrance name of the area level on Level Warp tiles that link to this area level. For example, when the player mouse hovers over a tile to warp to the area level, then this string is displayed.

fields.name: LevelEntry
fields.description: String Field. Used for displaying the UI popup title string when the player enters the area level.

fields.name: ObjGrp#
fields.description: Uses a numeric ID to define which possible Object Groups to spawn in this area level (See objgroup.txt). The game will go through each of these fields, so there can be more than 1 Object Group used in an area level. If this value equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: ObjPrb#
fields.description: Determines the random chance (out of 100) for each Object Group to spawn in the area level. This field depends on the related ObjGrp# field being defined.

fields.name: LevelGroup
fields.description: Defines what group this level belongs to. Used for condensing level names in desecrated (terror) zones messaging.

fields.name: PreventTownPortal
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then prevent town portals from being opened while in this level. If equals 0, then ignore this.

lowqualityitems.title: lowqualityitems.txt
lowqualityitems.overview:
Reference file that defines low quality item types.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Localized string key for the low quality item type.

lvlmaze.title: LvlMaze.txt
lvlmaze.overview:
This file controls the sizes of the underground area levels. This file uses the levels from levels.txt and specifies the sizes for each room, which can mean how many Level Presets to use to build out the entire randomly generated area.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Level
fields.description: This refers to the level area's Id (levels)

fields.name: Rooms
fields.description: Controls the total number of rooms that a Level Maze will generate when playing the game in Normal Difficulty, Nightmare Difficulty, and Hell Difficulty, respectively.

fields.name: SizeX
fields.description: Controls the length and width sizes of each room (ds1 map files) that is added to the Level Maze. This is measured in tile sizes.

fields.name: Merge
fields.description: This value affects the probability that a room gets an adjacent room linked next to it. This is a random chance out of 1000.

lvlprest.title: LvlPrest.txt
lvlprest.overview:
This file controls the values for each Level Preset. A Level Preset is a static area composed of tiles that is used to construct entire area levels found in the game.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Def
fields.description: Defines the unique numeric ID for the Level Preset. This is referenced in other files.

fields.name: LevelId
fields.description: This refers to the area level's Id (levels) field. If this value is not equal to 0, then this Level Preset is used to build that entire area level. If this value is equal to 0, then the Level Preset does not define the entire area level and is used as a part of constructing area levels.

fields.name: Populate
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then units are allowed to spawn in the Level Preset. If equals 0, then units will never spawn in the Level Preset.

fields.name: Logicals
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the Level Preset allow for wall transparency to function. If equals 0, then walls will always appear solid.

fields.name: Outdoors
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the Level Preset will be classified as an outdoor area, which can mean that lighting will function differently. If equals 0, then the Level Preset will be classified as an indoor area.

fields.name: Animate
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the game will animate the tiles in the Level Preset. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: KillEdge
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the game will remove tiles that border the size of the Level Preset. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: FillBlanks
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then all blank tiles in the Level Preset will be filled with unwalkable tiles. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: SizeX
fields.description: Specifies the Length and Width tile size values of the Level Preset, which are used for determining how big to build area levels. These values are equal to 0 for Level Presets that are static.

fields.name: automap
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this Level Preset will be automatically completely revealed on the Automap. If equals 0, then this Level Preset will be hidden on the Automap and will need to be explored.

fields.name: Scan
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this Level Preset will allow the usage of warping with waypoints (This requires that the Level Preset has a waypoint object). If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Pops
fields.description: Defines how many Pop tiles are defined in the Level Preset file. These Pop tiles are mainly used for controlling the roof and wall popping when a player enters a building in an area.

fields.name: PopPad
fields.description: Determines the size of the Pop tile area, by using an offset value. This offset value can increase or decrease the size of the Pop tile size if it has a positive or negative value.

fields.name: Files
fields.description: Determines the number of different versions to use for the Level Preset. This value acts as a range, which the game will use for randomly choosing one of the File# fields to build the Level Preset. This is how the Level Presets have variety when the area level is being built.

fields.name: File#
fields.description: Specifies the name of which ds1 file to use. The ds1 files contain data for building Level Presets. If this value equals 0, then this field will be ignored. The number of these defined fields should match the value used in the Files field.

fields.name: Dt1Mask
fields.description: This functions as a bit field mask with a size of a 32 bit value. This explains to the ds1 file which of the 32 dt1 tile 1, File2=2, File3 = 4, File4=8, File5=16...File32 = 2147483648). To build the Dt1Mask, you would select which File # (lvltypes) fields to use from and add their associated bit values together for a total value. This total value is the bitmask value.

lvlsub.title: LvlSub.txt
lvlsub.overview:
This file controls how tiles can be substituted in for other tiles. The game will divide the level into clusters and iterate through these clusters to randomly substitute tiles with different ones for more visual diversity.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: This refers to the SubType (levels) field. This defines a group that multiple substitutions can share.

fields.name: File
fields.description: Specifies the name of which ds1 file to use. The ds1 files contain data for building Level Presets.

fields.name: CheckAll
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then substitute each tile in the room. If equals 0, then substitute random tiles in the room.

fields.name: BordType
fields.description: This controls how often substituting tiles can work for border tiles
table: Single One Only. This allows substituting for 1 border in total
One Per Cluster. This allows substituting 1 border for each cluster in the level
Allow substituting borders for all of the level

fields.name: GridSize
fields.description: Controls the tile size of a cluster for substituting tiles. This evenly affects both the X and Y size values of a room.

fields.name: Dt1Mask
fields.description: This functions as a bit field mask with a size of a 32 bit value. This explains to the ds1 file which of the 32 dt1 tile 1, File2=2, File3 = 4, File4=8, File5=16...File32 = 2147483648). To build the Dt1Mask, you would select which File # (lvltypes) fields to use and add their associated bit values together for a total value. This total value is the bitmask value.

fields.name: Prob#
fields.description: This value affects the probability that the tile substitution is used. This is a random chance out of 100. Which Prob# field that is checked depends on the SubTheme (levels) value.

fields.name: Trials#
fields.description: Controls the number of times to randomly substitute tiles in a cluster. If this value equals -1, then the game will try to do as many tile substitutions that can be allowed based on the cluster and tile size. This field depends on the CheckAll field being equals to 0.

fields.name: Max#
fields.description: The maximum number of clusters of tiles to substitute randomly. This field depends on the CheckAll field being equals to 0.

lvltypes.title: LvlTypes.txt
lvltypes.overview:
This file controls which files containing tile graphics are used for creating maps. This looks at dt1 files, which contain tile images of the environments foundin the game. Each line in this file defines a Level Type and what files it uses.
The order of each Level Type defined in this file will convey what ID value it has, which is referenced by the following files: levels.txt, lvlprest.txt. The order of these Level Types should not be changed.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: File #
fields.description: Specifies the name of which dt1 file to use. The dt1 files contain the images for each area tile found in each Act. If this value equals 0, then this field will be ignored.

fields.name: Act
fields.description: Defines which Act is related to the Level Type. When loading an Act, the game will only use the Level Types associated with that Act number. Uses a decimal number to convey each Act number (Ex: A value of 3 means Act 3)

lvlwarp.title: LvlWarp.txt
lvlwarp.overview:
This file controls how the player is moved to different area levels, such as entrances and exits between different areas. This player transportation of between levels is defined as a Level Warp. Level Warps function as special tiles that are added to the area for controlling the location for where to transport the player.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: This is a reference field to define the Level Warp

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Defines the numeric ID for the type of Level Warp. This ID can be shared between multiple Level Warps if those Level Warps want to use the same functionality. This is referenced in other files.

fields.name: SelectX
fields.description: These values define the horizontal and vertical offsets (respectively) of the starting left corner position of the Level Warp area. This is treated as the starting position to select the interactable Level Warp area in the area level. This value is measured in pixels.

fields.name: SelectDX
fields.description: These values define the horizontal and vertical offsets (respectively) of the offset from the starting position of the Level Warp area. This is added with the SelectX & SelectY fields (respectively) to determine the overall size and position of the Level Warp in the area level. This value is measured in pixels.

fields.name: ExitWalkX
fields.description: These values define the horizontal and vertical positions (respectively) of the destination location where the player will walk to after exiting to this Level Warp. This value is measured with a sub-tile offset from the base position of the Level Warp. One full tile on a level is composed of a grid of 5x5 sub-tiles.

fields.name: OffsetX
fields.description: These values define the horizontal and vertical positions (respectively) of the sub-tile for the Level Warp, where the player will appear when exiting to this area level. This value is measured with a sub-tile offset from the base position of the Level Warp. One full tile on a level is composed of a grid of 5x5 sub-tiles.

fields.name: LitVersion
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then Level Warp tiles will change their appearance when highlighted. If equals 0, then the Level Warp tiles will not change appearance when highlighted.

fields.name: Tiles
fields.description: Defines an index offset to determine which tile to use in the tile set for the highlighted version of the Level Warp. These tiles are loaded and hidden/revealed when the player mouse hovers over the Level Warp tiles. This relies on LitVersion being enabled.

fields.name: NoInteract
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the Level Warp cannot be directly interacted by the player. If equals 0, then the player can interact with the Level Warp.

fields.name: Direction
fields.description: Defines the orientation of the Level Warp. Uses a specific string code.
table: Left. If this is selected, then the tile type direction should match this.
Right. If this is selected, then the tile type direction should match this.
Both. This can mean that the Level Warp can be reassigned its direction.

fields.name: UniqueId
fields.description: Defines the unique numeric ID for the Level Warp. Each Level Warp should have a unique ID so that the game can handle loading that specific Level Warp's related files.

magicprefix.title: MagicPrefix.txt
magicprefix.overview:
This file controls what item affixes (groups of item modifiers) are applied as the prefix for an itemThese item affixes will appear at the start of an item's name.
This file is loaded together with other similar files in the following order: MagicSuffix.txt, magicprefix.txt, automagic.txt. These combined files form the Item Mods structure.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Defines the item affix name.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Defines which game version to use this item affix (<100 = Classic mode | 100 = Expansion mode).

fields.name: spawnable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item affix is used as part of the game's randomizer for assigning item modifiers when an item spawns. If equals 0, then this item affix is never used.

fields.name: rare
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item affix can be used when randomly assigning item modifiers when a rare item spawns. If equals 0, then this item affix is not used for rare items.

fields.name: level
fields.description: The minimum item level required for this item affix to spawn on the item. If the item level is below this value, then the item affix will not spawn on the item.

fields.name: maxlevel
fields.description: The maximum item level required for this item affix to spawn on the item. If the item level is above this value, then the item affix will not spawn on the item.

fields.name: levelreq
fields.description: The minimum character level required to equip an item that has this item affix

fields.name: classspecific
fields.description: Controls if this item affix should only be used for class specific items. This relies on the class code specified in Class (itemtypes), for the specific item.

fields.name: class
fields.description: Controls which character class is required for the class specific level requirement defined by classlevelreq.

fields.name: classlevelreq
fields.description: The minimum character level required for a specific class in order to equip an item that has this item affix. This relies on the class specified in the class field. If equals null, then the class will default to using the levelreq field.

fields.name: frequency
fields.description: Controls the probability that the affix appears on the item (a higher value means that the item affix will appear on the item more often). This value gets summed together with other frequency values from all possible item affixes that can spawn on the item, and then is used as a denominator value for the randomizer. Whichever item affix is randomly selected will be the one to appear on the item. The formula is calculated as the following: [Item Affix Selected] = [frequency] / [Total Frequency]. If the item has a magic level (from magic lvl (armor), magic lvl (weapons), or magic lvl (misc)) then the magic level value is multiplied with this value. If equals 0, then this item affix will never appear on an item.

fields.name: group
fields.description: Assigns an item affix to a specific group number. Items cannot spawn with more than 1 item affix with the same group number. This is used to guarantee that certain item affixes do not overlap on the same item. If this field is null, then the group number will default to group 0.

fields.name: mod#code
fields.description: Controls the item properties for the item affix.
fields.format: References a code (properties) or a code (PropertyGroups)

fields.name: mod#param
fields.description: The parameter value associated with the related property (mod#code). Usage depends on the property function (See func# (properties)).
fields.format: A number or references skill (skills), type (montype), or state (states)

fields.name: mod#min
fields.description: The min value to assign to the listed related (mod#code). Usage depends on the property function (See func# (properties)).

fields.name: mod#max
fields.description: The max value to assign to the listed related (mod#code). Usage depends on the property function (See func# (properties)).

fields.name: transformcolor
fields.description: Controls the color change of the item after spawning with this item affix. If empty, then the item affix will not change the item's color.

fields.name: itype#
fields.description: Controls what Item Types are allowed to spawn with this item affix.

fields.name: etype#
fields.description: Controls what Item Types are forbidden to spawn with this item affix.

fields.name: multiply
fields.description: Multiplicative modifier for the item's buy and sell costs, based on the item affix (Calculated in 1024ths for buy cost and 4096ths for sell cost).

fields.name: add
fields.description: Flat integer modification to the item's buy and sell costs, based on the item affix.

magicsuffix.title: MagicSuffix.txt
magicsuffix.overview:
This file controls what item affixes (groups of item modifiers) are applied as the suffix for an item. These item affixes will appear at the end of the items name

misc.title: misc.txt
misc.overview:
This file controls the functionalities for miscellaneous type items, such as the non-weapons and non-armor items. This file is loaded together with other similar files in the following order: weapons.txt, armor.txt, misc.txt. These combined files form the items structure. Technically these files share the same fields, but some fields are exclusive for specific item types, so they are not displayed in the data files that do not need them. These are the fields exclusive to this file.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: autobelt
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item will automatically be placed is a free slot in the belt when picked up, if possible. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: BetterGem
fields.description: Links to another item's "code" field. Used by the function 18 in the Code (shrines) field to know what a selected gem's upgrade will be when the player uses the gem shrine.

fields.name: multibuy
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then use the multi-buy transaction function when holding the shift key and buying this item from an NPC store. This multi-buy function will automatically purchase enough of the item to fill up to a full quantity stack or fill the available belt slots if the item is has the autobelt field enabled. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: spellicon
fields.description: Determines the icon asset for displaying the item's spell. This uses an ID value based on the global skillicon file. If this value equals -1, then the item's spell will not display an icon. Used as a parameter for a pSpell function.

fields.name: pSpell
fields.description: Uses an ID value to select a spell function when the item is used. This depends on the item type.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Signifies what state will be applied to the player when the item is used. Used as a parameter for a pSpell function.

fields.name: cstate#
fields.description: Signifies what state will be removed from the player when the item is used. Used as a parameter for a pSpell function.

fields.name: len
fields.description: Calculates the frame length of a state. Used as a parameter for a pSpell function.
fields.format: Item scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: stat#
fields.description: Controls the stat modifier when the item is used. Used as a parameter for a pSpell function.

fields.name: calc#
fields.description: Calculates the value of the relative stat# field. Used as a parameter for a pSpell function.
fields.format: Item scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: spelldesc

fields.name: spelldescstr
fields.description: String Key. Used as a parameter for the spelldesc function.

fields.name: spelldesccalc
fields.description: Calculates the numeric equation. Used as a parameter for the spelldesc function.
fields.format: Item scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: spelldesccolor
fields.description: Uses a code number to change the color of the string used in the spelldesc function.

fields.name: AdvancedStashStackable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then marks the item as being stackable in the dedicated shared stash tab.

fields.name: UsageConditionCalc
fields.description: If the evaluated result of this BBE is 0, then prevent the item from being used and display the name in red.
fields.format: Item scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: version
fields.description: Defines which game version to create this item (0 = Classic mode | 100 = Expansion mode).

fields.name: compactsave
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then only the item's base stats will be stored in the character save, but not any modifiers or additional stats. If equals 0, then all of the items stats will be saved.

fields.name: rarity
fields.description: Determines the chance that the item will randomly spawn (1/#). The higher the value then the rarer the item will be. This field depends on the spawnable field being enabled, the quest field being disabled, and the item level being less than or equal to the area level. This value is also affected by the relative Act number that the item is dropping in, where the higher the Act number, then the more common the item will drop.

fields.name: spawnable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item can be randomly spawned. If equals 0, then this item will never randomly spawn.

fields.name: DropConditionCalc
fields.description: If the evaluated result of this condition is 0, then prevent the item from being randomly dropped in treasure classes.
fields.format: Treasure Class scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: speed
fields.description: If the item type is an armor, then this will affect the Walk/Run Speed reduction when wearing the armor. If the item type is a weapon, then this will affect the Attack Speed reduction when wearing the weapon.

fields.name: reqstr
fields.description: Defines the amount of the Strength attribute needed to use the item.

fields.name: reqdex
fields.description: Defines the amount of the Dexterity attribute needed to use the item.

fields.name: durability
fields.description: Defines the base durability amount that the item will spawn with.

fields.name: nodurability
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item will not have durability. If equals 0, then the item will have durability.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Controls the base item level. This is used for determining when the item is allowed to drop, such as making sure that the item level is not greater than the monster's level or the area level.

fields.name: ShowLevel
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then display the item level next to the item name. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: levelreq
fields.description: Controls the player level requirement for being able to use the item.

fields.name: cost
fields.description: Defines the base gold cost of the item when being sold by an NPC. This can be affected by item modifiers and the rarity of the item.

fields.name: gamble cost
fields.description: Defines the gambling gold cost of the item on the Gambling UI.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Defines a unique 3 letter/number code for the item. This is used as an identifier to reference the item.

fields.name: namestr
fields.description: String Key that is used for the base item name.

fields.name: magic lvl
fields.description: Defines the magic level of the item, which can affect how magical item modifiers that can appear on the item (See automagic.txt).

fields.name: auto prefix
fields.description: Automatically picks an item affix name from a designated group (automagic) value, instead of using random prefixes. This is only used when the item is Magical quality.

fields.name: alternategfx
fields.description: Uses a unique 3 letter/number code similar to the defined code fields to determine what in-game graphics to display on the player character when the item is equipped.

fields.name: normcode
fields.description: Links to a code field to determine the normal version of the item

fields.name: ubercode
fields.description: Links to a code field to determine the Exceptional version of the item

fields.name: ultracode
fields.description: Links to a code field to determine the Elite version of the item

fields.name: component
fields.description: Determines the layer of player animation when the item is equipped. This uses a code referenced from the Composit.txt file.

fields.name: invwidth
fields.description: Defines the width of grid cells that the item occupies in the player inventory.

fields.name: invheight
fields.description: Defines the height of grid cells that the item occupies in the player inventory.

fields.name: hasinv
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item will have its own inventory allowing for the capability to socket gems, runes, or jewels. If equals 0, then the item cannot have sockets.

fields.name: gemsockets
fields.description: Controls the maximum number of sockets allowed on this item. This is limited by the item's size based on the invwidth and invheight fields. This also compares with MaxSockets# (itemtypes).

fields.name: gemapplytype
fields.description: Determines which affect from a gem or rune will be applied when it is socketed into this item (See gems.txt).

fields.name: flippyfile
fields.description: Controls which DC6 file to use for displaying the item in the game world when it is dropped on the ground (uses the file name as the input).

fields.name: invfile
fields.description: Controls which DC6 file to use for displaying the item graphics in the inventory (uses the file name as the input).

fields.name: uniqueinvfile
fields.description: Controls which DC6 file to use for displaying the item graphics in the inventory when it is a Unique quality item (uses the file name as the input).

fields.name: setinvfile
fields.description: Controls which DC6 file to use for displaying the item graphics in the inventory when it is a Set quality item (uses the file name as the input).

fields.name: useable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item can be used with the right-click mouse button command (this only works with specific belt items or quest items). If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: stackable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item will use a quantity field and handle stacking functionality. This can depend on if the item type is throwable, is a type of ammunition, or is some other kind of miscellaneous item. If equals 0, then the item cannot be stacked.

fields.name: minstack
fields.description: Controls the minimum stack count or quantity that is allowed on the item. This field depends on the stackable field being enabled.

fields.name: maxstack
fields.description: Controls the maximum stack count or quantity that is allowed on the item. This field depends on the stackable field being enabled.

fields.name: spawnstack
fields.description: Controls the stack count or quantity that the item can spawn with. This field depends on the stackable field being enabled.

fields.name: Transmogrify
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item will use the transmogrify function. If equals 0, then ignore this. This field depends on the useable field being enabled.

fields.name: TMogType
fields.description: Links to a code field to determine which item is chosen to transmogrify this item to.

fields.name: TMogMin
fields.description: Controls the minimum quantity that the transmogrify item will have. This depends on what item was chosen in the TMogType field, and that the transmogrify item has quantity.

fields.name: TMogMax
fields.description: Controls the maximum quantity that the transmogrify item will have. This depends on what item was chosen in the TMogType field, and that the transmogrify item has quantity.

fields.name: type
fields.description: This is the item's type, which controls how the item functions.

fields.name: type2
fields.description: Secondary item type. This is optional but can add more functionalities and possibilities with the item.

fields.name: dropsound
fields.description: Sound used when the item is dropped on the ground.

fields.name: dropsfxframe
fields.description: Defines which frame in the flippyfile animation to play the dropsound sound when the item is dropped on the ground.

fields.name: usesound
fields.description: Sound used when the item is moved in the inventory or used.

fields.name: unique
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item can only spawn as a Unique quality type. If equals 0, then the item can spawn as other quality types.

fields.name: transparent
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item will be drawn transparent on the player model (similar to ethereal models). If equals 0, then the item will appear solid on the player model.

fields.name: transtbl
fields.description: Controls what type of transparency to use, based on the transparent field being enabled. Corresponds to a ETRANSTYPE (enums).

fields.name: lightradius
fields.description: Controls the value of the light radius that this item can apply on the monster. This only affects monsters with this item equipped, not other types of units. This is ignored if the item's component on the monster is "lit", "med", or "hvy".

fields.name: belt
fields.description: Controls which belt type to use for belt items only. This field determines what index entry in the belts.txt file to use.

fields.name: quest
fields.description: Controls what quest class is tied to the item which can enable certain item functionalities for a specific quest. Any value greater than 0 will also mean the item is flagged as a quest item, which can affect how it is displayed in tooltips, how it is traded with other players, its item rarity, and how it cannot be sold to an NPC. If equals 0, then the item will not be flagged as a quest item.
table: Respec from Akara Complete, Act 5 Prologue

fields.name: questdiffcheck
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1 and the quest field is enabled, then the game will check the current difficulty setting and will tie that difficulty setting to the quest item. This means that the player can have more than 1 of the same quest item as long each they are obtained per difficulty mode (Normal / Nightmare / Hell). If equals 0 and the quest field is enabled, then the player can only have 1 count of the quest item in the inventory, regardless of difficulty.

fields.name: missiletype
fields.description: Points to an entry's index in missiles.txt, which determines what type of missile is used when using the throwing weapons

fields.name: durwarning
fields.description: Controls the threshold value for durability to display the low durability warning UI. This is only used if the item has durability.

fields.name: qntwarning
fields.description: Controls the threshold value for quantity to display the low quantity warning UI. This is only used if the item has stacks.

fields.name: mindam
fields.description: The minimum physical damage provided by the item.

fields.name: maxdam
fields.description: The maximum physical damage provided by the item.

fields.name: StrBonus
fields.description: The percentage multiplier that gets multiplied the player's current Strength attribute value to modify the bonus damage percent from the equipped item. If this equals 1, then default the value to 100.

fields.name: DexBonus
fields.description: The percentage multiplier that gets multiplied the player's current Dexterity attribute value to modify the bonus damage percent from the equipped item. If this equals 1, then default the value to 100.

fields.name: gemoffset
fields.description: Determines the starting index offset for reading the gems.txt file when determining what effects gems or runes will have the item based on the gemapplytype field. For example, if this value equals 9, then the game will start with index 9 ("Chipped Emerald") and ignore the previously defined gems in the gems.txt file, which can mean that those ignored gems will not apply modifiers when socketed into the item.

fields.name: bitfield1
fields.description: Controls different flags that can affect the item. Uses an integer value to check against different bit fields by using the "&" operator. For example, if the value equals 5 (binary = 101) then that returns true for both the 4 (binary = 100) and 1 (binary = 1) bit field values.
bits: Allow the item to be capable of having Magic quality
The item is classified as metal
The item is classified as a spellcaster item (currently does nothing)
The item is classified as a skill based item (currently does nothing)

fields.name: NPCMin
fields.description: Minimum amount of this item type in Normal rarity that the NPC can sell at once.

fields.name: NPCMax
fields.description: Maximum amount of this item type in Normal rarity that the NPC can sell at once. This must be equal to or greater than the minimum amount.

fields.name: NPCMagicMin
fields.description: Minimum amount of this item type in Magical rarity that the NPC can sell at once

fields.name: NPCMagicMax
fields.description: Maximum amount of this item type in Magical rarity that the NPC can sell at once. This must be equal to or greater than the minimum amount.

fields.name: NPCMagicLvl
fields.description: Maximum magic level allowed for this item type in Magical rarity.

fields.name: Transform
fields.description: Controls the color palette change of the item for the character model graphics. Corresponds to a EITRANSFORMCLASS (enums).

fields.name: InvTrans
fields.description: Controls the color palette change of the item for the inventory graphics. Corresponds to a EITRANSFORMCLASS (enums).

fields.name: SkipName
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1 and the item is Unique rarity, then skip adding the item's base name in its title. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: NightmareUpgrade
fields.description: Links to another item's code field. Used to determine which item will replace this item when being generated in the NPC's store while the game is playing in Nightmare difficulty. If this field's code equals "xxx", then this item will not change in this difficulty.

fields.name: HellUpgrade
fields.description: Links to another item's code field. Used to determine which item will replace this item when being generated in the NPC's store while the game is playing in Hell difficulty. If this field's code equals "xxx", then this item will not change in this difficulty.

fields.name: Nameable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the item's name can be personalized by Anya for the Act 5 Betrayal of Harrogath quest reward. If equals 0, then the item cannot be used for the personalized name reward.

fields.name: PermStoreItem
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item will always appear on the NPC's store. If equals 0, then the item will randomly appear on the NPC's store when appropriate.

fields.name: EventItem
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then this item will have its named colored with the FONTCOLOR (enums) "EventItemsColor".

fields.name: UICatOverride
fields.description: Allows this item to override what UI Category it should use (for loot filter and chronicle uniques page). If there's no override, this item will belong to the category that its type1 field uses. If Null, this item will be excluded from lootfilter / chronicle. If a valid UI Category, this item will belong to that UI category instead of the one its type would usually put it in.

fields.name: diablocloneweight
fields.description: The amount of weight added to the diablo clone progress when this item is sold. When offline, selling this item will instead immediately spawn diablo clone.
