fields.description: Controls the amount of sub tiles that the object occupies using X and Y coordinates. This is generally used for measuring the object's size when trying to spawn objects in rooms and controlling their distances apart.

fields.name: FrameCnt#
fields.description: Controls the frame length of the object's mode. If this equals 0, then that mode will be skipped. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: FrameDelta#
fields.description: Controls the animation frame rate of how many frames to update per delta (Measured in 256ths). Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: CycleAnim#
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object's current animation will loop back to play again when it finishes. If equals 0, then the object will generally play the Opened mode after playing the Operating mode. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: Lit#
fields.description: Controls the Light Radius distance value for the object. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: BlocksLight#
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object will draw a shadow. If equals 0, then the object will not draw a shadow. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: HasCollision#
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object will have collision. If equals 0, then the object will not have collision, and units can walk through it. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: IsAttackable0
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the player can target this object to be attacked, and the player will use the Kick skill when operating the object. If the object has the Class equal to "CompellingOrb" or "SoulStoneForge", then instead of using the Kick skill, players will use the Attack skill when operating the object. If equals 0, then ignore this, and the player will not use a skill or animation when operating the object.

fields.name: Start#
fields.description: Controls the frame for where the object will start playing the next animation.

fields.name: EnvEffect
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then enable the object to update its mode based on the game's time of day. This can mean that when the object is spawned, and it is current day time and the object is in Opened or Operating mode, then it will reset back to Neutral mode. Also, if the current time is dusk, night, or dawn and the object is in Neutral mode, then it will change to Operating mode. If equals 0, then the object will not update its mode based on the time of day.

fields.name: IsDoor
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object will be treated as a door when the game handles its collision, animation properties, tooltips, and commands. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: BlocksVis
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object will block the player's line of sight to see anything beyond the object. If equals 0, then ignore this. This field relies on the IsDoor field being enabled.

fields.name: Orientation
fields.description: Determines the object's orientation type, which can affect mouse selection priority of the object when a unit is being rendered in front of or behind the object (such as a door object covering a unit and how the mouse selection should handle that). This also affects the randomization of the coordinates when spawning the object near the edge of a room.

fields.name: OrderFlag#
fields.description: Controls how the object's sprite is drawn, which can affect how it is displayed in Perspective game camera mode. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: PreOperate
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then enable a random chance that the object will spawn in already in Opened mode. The game will choose a 1/14 chance that this can happen when the object is spawned. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Mode#
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then confirm that this object has the correlating mode. If equals 0, then this object will not have the correlating mode. This flag can affect how the object functions work. Each field is numbered, correlating to 1 of 8 Object Modes that the object uses (See Token (ObjMode)).

fields.name: Xoffset
fields.description: Controls the offset values in the X and Y directions for the object's visual graphics. This is measured in game pixels.

fields.name: Draw
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then draw the object's shadows. If equal's 0, then do not draw the object's shadows.

fields.name: Red
fields.description: Controls the Red color gradient of the object's Light Radius. This field depends on the Lit# field having a value greater than 0.

fields.name: Green
fields.description: Controls the Green color gradient of the object's Light Radius. This field depends on the Lit# field having a value greater than 0.

fields.name: Blue
fields.description: Controls the Blue color gradient of the object's Light Radius. This field depends on the Lit# field having a value greater than 0.

fields.name: COMP
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object will be flagged to have a specific composite piece, and the game will use the component system to handle the object's mouse selection collision box. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: TotalPieces
fields.description: Defines the total amount of composite pieces. If this value is greater than 1, then the game will treat the object with the multiple composite piece system, and the player can hover the mouse over and select the object's different components.

fields.name: SubClass
fields.description: Determines the object's class type by declaring a specific value. This is used by the various functions (InitFn, OperateFn, PopulateFn) for knowing how to handle specific types of objects.

fields.name: Xspace
fields.description: Controls the X and Y distance delta values between adjacent objects when they are being populated together. This field is only used by the Populate Function (PopulateFn) values 3 and 4, for the Add Barrels and Add Crates functions.

fields.name: NameOffset
fields.description: Controls the vertical offset of the name tooltip's position above the object when the object is being selected. This is measured in pixels.

fields.name: MonsterOK
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then if a monster operates the object, then the object will run its operate function. If equals 0, then then if a monster operates the object, then the object will not run its operate function.

fields.name: ShrineFunction
fields.description: Controls what shrine function to use (See the Code (shrines) field) when the object is told to do its Skill command.

fields.name: Restore
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, the game will restore the object in an inactive state when the area level repopulates after a player loads back into it. If equals 0, then the game will not restore the object.

fields.name: Parm#
fields.description: Used as possible parameters for various functions for the object

fields.name: Lockable
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object will have a random chance to spawn with the locked attribute and have a display tooltip name with the "lockedchest" string key. This only works when the object has the Init Function (InitFn) value equal to 3. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Gore
fields.description: Controls if an object should call its Populate function (PopulateFn) when it is chosen as an object that can spawn in a room. Objects with a gore value greater than 2 will not be populated in rooms.

fields.name: Sync
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the object's animation rate will always match the FrameDelta# field (depending on the object's mode) which means the client and server will have synced animations. If equals 0, then the animation rate will have random visual variation.

fields.name: Damage
fields.description: Controls the amount of damage dealt by the object when it performs an Operate Function (OperateFn) that deals damage such as triggering a pulse trap or an explosion.

fields.name: overlay
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then add and remove an overlay on the object based on its current mode. If equals 0, then ignore this. This field will only work with specific object Classes and will use specific Overlays for those objects.

fields.name: CollisionSubst
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the game will handle the bounding box around the object for mouse selection. The game will use the object's pixel size and Left, Top, Width, Height field values to determine the collision size. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: Left
fields.description: Controls the starting X position offset value for drawing the bounding collision box around the object for mouse selection. This field depends on the CollisionSubst field being enabled.

fields.name: Top
fields.description: Controls the starting Y position offset value for drawing the bounding collision box around the object for mouse selection. This field depends on the CollisionSubst field being enabled.

fields.name: Width
fields.description: Controls the ending X position offset value for drawing the bounding collision box around the object for mouse selection. This field depends on the CollisionSubst field being enabled.

fields.name: Height
fields.description: Controls the ending Y position offset value for drawing the bounding collision box around the object for mouse selection. This field depends on the CollisionSubst field being enabled.

fields.name: automap

objgroup.title: objgroup.txt
objgroup.overview:
This file controls what group of possible Objects to spawn in a part of an area level. The order of each Object Group defined in this file will convey what ID value it has, which is referenced by the levels.txt file. The order of these Object Groups should not be changed.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: ID#
fields.description: Uses references the index of an object from %!objects!%, which assigns an Object to this Object Group

fields.name: DENSITY#
fields.description: Controls the number of Objects to spawn in the area level. This is also affected by the Object's populate function defined by the %!objects#PopulateFn!$ field. The maximum value allowed is 128.

fields.name: PROB#
fields.description: Controls the probability that the Object will spawn in the area level. This is calculated in order so the first probability that is successful will be chosen. This also means that these field values should add up to exactly 100 in total to guarantee that one of the objects spawn.

Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Token

objpreset.title: objpreset.txt

Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: Index
fields.description: Assigns a unique numeric ID to the Object Preset so that it can be properly referenced

fields.name: Act
fields.description: Defines the Act number used for each Object Preset. Uses values between 1 to 5.

fields.name: ObjectClass
fields.description: Assigns an Object to this Object Preset

overlay.title: Overlay.txt
overlay.overview:
This file controls the overlay graphics related to states, auras, cast animations, curses, and buffs.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: overlay
fields.description: Defines the name of the overlay, used in other data files

fields.name: Filename
fields.description: Defines which DCC file to use for the Overlay

fields.name: version
fields.description: Defines which game version to use this Overlay (0 = Classic mode | 100 = Expansion mode)

fields.name: Character
fields.description: Used for name categorizing Overlays for unit translation mapping

fields.name: PreDraw
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then display the Overlay in front of sprites. If equals 0, then display the Overlay behind sprites.

fields.name: 1ofN
fields.description: Controls how to randomly display Overlays. This value will randomly add to the current index of the Overlay to possibly use another Overlay that is indexed after this current Overlay. The formula is as follows: Index = Index + RANDOM(0, [1ofN]-1).

fields.name: Xoffset
fields.description: Sets the horizontal offset of the overlay on the unit. Positive values move it toward the left and negative values move it towards the right.

fields.name: Yoffset
fields.description: Sets the vertical offset of the overlay on the unit. Positive values move it down and negative values move it up.

fields.name: Height#
fields.description: These are additional values added to Yoffset. Only 1 of these Height# fields are added, and which field that gets selected depends on the OverlayHeight (monstats2) field value (Example: If the OverlayHeight (monstats2) value is 4, then use the Height4 field). If the OverlayHeight (monstats2) value is 0, then ignore these Height# fields and add a default value of 75 to Yoffset. Player unit types will always use Height2.

fields.name: AnimRate
fields.description: Controls the animation frame rate of the Overlay. The value is the number of frames that will update per second.

fields.name: LoopWaitTime
fields.description: Controls the number of periodic frames to wait until redrawing the Overlay. This only works with Overlays that are a loop type.

fields.name: Trans
fields.description: Controls the alpha mode for how the Overlay is displayed, which can affect transparency and blending

fields.name: InitRadius
fields.description: Controls the starting Light Radius value for the Overlay (Max = 18)

fields.name: Radius
fields.description: Controls the maximum Light Radius value for the Overlay. This can only be greater than or equal to InitRadius. If greater than InitRadius, then the Light Radius will increase in size per frame, starting from InitRadius until it matches the Radius value (Max = 18)

fields.name: Red
fields.description: Controls the Red color gradient of the Light Radius

fields.name: Green
fields.description: Controls the Green color gradient of the Light Radius

fields.name: Blue
fields.description: Controls the Blue color gradient of the Light Radius

fields.name: NumDirections
fields.description: The number of directions in the cell file

fields.name: LocalBlood
fields.description: Controls how to display green blood or VFX on a unit.
table: Transform the default red blood splatter to green blood
Change the monster palette to green

fields.name: WeaponStateFlags
fields.description: Controls a bit field flag where each value specifies which state the overlay can react to (used for vfx).

fields.name: WeaponStateGroup
fields.description: Specify a filter to have the overlay react only for states that belong to the specified group.

fields.name: StartSound
fields.description: Optional sound to play when the overlay is started.

pettype.title: pettype.txt
pettype.overview:
This file controls the various statistics for each type of pet from all the classes summon Skills.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: pet type
fields.description: Defines the name of the pet type.

fields.name: group
fields.description: Used as an ID field, where if pet types share the same group value, then only 1 pet of that group is allowed to be alive at any time. If equals 0 (or null), then ignore this.

fields.name: pool
fields.description: Marks a pet type as belonging to a pool. Pets from all pet types in the pool share the max amount of pets active. Individual pet types are still constrained by their own max. For example, if "demon" and "bind demon" are in the same pool, a pet of type "bind demon" will take up a slot in the "demon" pet type's max, the pool will have a max of 3, allowing for 2 "demon" and 1 "bind demon".

fields.name: basemax
fields.description: This sets a baseline maximum number of pets allowed to be alive when skill levels are reset or changed.

fields.name: warp
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then the Pet will teleport to the player when the player teleports or warps to another area. If equals 0, then the pet will die instead.

fields.name: range
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then the Pet will die if the player teleports or warps to another area and is located more than 40 grid tiles in distances from the Pet. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: partysend
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then tell the Pet to do the Party Location Update command (find the location of its Player) when its health changes. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: unsummon
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then the Pet can be unsummoned by the Unsummon skill function. If equals 0, then the Pet cannot be unsummoned.

fields.name: automap
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then display the Pet on the Automap. If equals 0, then hide the pet on the Automap.

fields.name: name
fields.description: String Key. Used to define the Pet's name on its party frame

fields.name: drawhp
fields.description: Boolean field. If equals 1, then display the Pet's Life bar under the party frame. If equals 0, then hide the Pet's Life bar under the party icon.

fields.name: icontype
fields.description: Controls the functionality for how to display the Pet Icon and number of Pets counter
table: Do not display the Pet icon
Display the Pet icon and do not show the Pet counter
Display the Pet icon and show the Pet counter
Display individual icons for each Pet of this type. Do not show the Pet counter.

· Requires the stat's "max" value as the skill's level. If that level is 0 then level equals "clamp("item level" - reqlevel (skills)) / 4 + 1, 1, maxlvl (skills))". If that level is below 0 then level equals "max(1, ("item level" - reqlevel (skills)) / max(1, max(1, 99 - reqlevel (skills)) / -level))"
Uses the stat's "min" and "max" value as a random selection of the stat's "parameter" value

· Always sets the current durability to its maximum durability after the calculation of the stat value

· Determines the number of sockets on an item
· If the stat has "min" and "max" values, then calculate a random number of sockets between these values. Otherwise, use the stat's "parameter" value as the number of sockets
· The max number of sockets depends on the stat's "max" size, the item's inventory grid size, or the hard cap of 6 sockets maximum

· Always use the stat's "min" value
· If the stat is physical minimum damage, then set the item's minimum damage to the stat's value. Otherwise, simply set the stat's value to its "min" value.

· Use the stat's "parameter" value. Otherwise, calculate a random value between the stat's "min" and "max" value. Otherwise, use 0.· If the stat is physical maximum damage, then set the item's maximum damage to the stat's value

· Modifies the stat based on the current game's time of day, and the stat's preferred time period. The closer the current game's time of day is to the stat's preferred time period, then the stronger the stat's value will be, based on its "min" and "max" values
· Requires the stat's "parameter" value as the time period. The allowed time periods are:
o 0 = Day
o 1 = Dusk
o 2 = Night
o 3 = Dawn

· Used for creating a stat for a charged skill.
· Requires the stat's "parameter" value as the skill ID
· Requires the stat's "min" value to calculate the value MaxCharges (maximum number of charges)
o If that value equals 0, then default to 5 max charges
o If that value is less than 0, then equal to the following calculation: "MaxCharges = |MaxCharges| + |MaxCharges| * [CURRENT ITEM LEVEL] / 8"
o MaxCharges cannot exceed 255
· Requires the stat's "max" value as the skill's level
· The spawned number of charges is calculated as the following: "Random(0 and (MaxCharges - MaxCharges / 8)) + MaxCharges / 8 + 1"

table: Additional Set item properties will function like normal item properties, ignoring the Set

Additional Set item properties will be added depending the number of related Set items equipped. For example, if 2 Set items are equipped, then the aprop1a, aprop1b, aprop2a, and aprop2b fields will be added to the Set item.

skills.title: skills.txt
skills.overview:
This file controls all skill functionalities. Skills are abilities used by all units in the game.
Any column field name starting with "*" is considered a comment field and is not used by the game.

fields.name: skill
fields.description: Defines the unique name ID for the skill, which is how other files can reference the skill. The order of the defined skills will determine their ID numbers, so they should not be reordered.

fields.name: charclass

fields.name: skilldesc

fields.name: srvstopfunc
fields.description: Server Stop function. This controls how the skill cleans up after ending. This uses a code value to call a function, affecting how certain fields are used.
table: Handles changing the collision, pathing, and aura state of the caster.

fields.name: prgstack
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then all srvprgfunc# functions will execute, based on the current number of progressive charges. If equals 0, then only the relative srvprgfunc# function will execute, based on the current number of progressive charges.

fields.name: srvprgfunc#
fields.description: Controls what Server Do function is used when executing the progressive skill with a charge number equal to 1, 2, and 3, respectively. This field uses the same functions as the srvdofunc field.

fields.name: prgcalc#
fields.description: Calculation Field. Used as a possible parameter for calculating values when executing the progressive skill with a charge number equal to 1, 2, and 3, respectively.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: prgdam
fields.description: Calls a function to modify the progressive damage dealt
table: Modify the percentage of the physical damage dealt by "calc1 * aurastat1" and apply tgtoverlay on the target. For tooltips the bonus is calculated as "(skillcalc.txt identifier "ln12") * aurastat1"

Modify the percentage of the life steal and mana steal gained by the value of aurastat1
1: "life steal + calc1"
2: "life steal + calc1" and "mana steal + calc1"
3: "life steal + (2 * calc1)" and "mana steal + (2 * calc1)"
Add the skill's elemental damage (see EMin and related fields). If EType equals Cold, then when aurastat1 equals 2 or 3, add "Cold Length / Param2" to the Freeze Length

Add the skill's elemental damage (see EMin and related fields). If EType equals Cold, then when aurastat1 equals 3, add "Cold Length / Param5" to the Freeze Length. Convert a calc1 percentage of the physical damage dealt to the skill's elemental damage.

fields.name: srvmissile
fields.description: Used as a parameter for controlling the main missile used by the server functions.

fields.name: decquant
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the unit's ammo quantity will be updated each time the skill's srvdofunc is called. If equals 0, then ignore this.

fields.name: lob
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then missiles created by the skill's functions will use the missile lobbing function, which will cause the missile fly in an arc pattern. If equals 0, then missiles that are created will use the normal linear function.

fields.name: srvmissile#
fields.description: Used as a parameter for controlling the secondary missiles used by the server functions.

fields.name: useServerMissilesOnRemoteClients
fields.description: Control new missile changes per player skill. Values of 1 will force enable it for that skill. Skills that have matching server/client missiles sets for the skill get auto enabled. Setting this to a value greater than 1 will force it to skip this auto enable logic. If equals 0, then ignore this. Note: this feature is disabled.

fields.name: srvoverlay
fields.description: Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions to create an overlay on units.

fields.name: aurafilter
fields.description: Controls different flags that affect how the skill's aura will affect the different types of units. Uses an integer value to check against different bit fields. For example, if the value equals 4354 (binary = 1000100000010) then that returns true for the 4096 (binary = 1000000000000), 256 (binary = 0000100000000), and 2 (binary = 0000000000010) bit field values.

fields.name: aurastate
fields.description: A state applied to the caster unit. Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions.

fields.name: auratargetstate
fields.description: A state applied to the target unit. Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions.

fields.name: auralencalc
fields.description: Calculation Field. Controls the state duration on the unit (where 25 Frames = 1 second). If this value is empty, then the state duration will be controlled by other functions, or it will last forever. Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: aurarangecalc
fields.description: Calculation Field. Controls the area radius size for auras and other effects, measured in grid sub-tiles. Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: aurastat#
fields.description: Controls which stat modifiers will be altered or added by the skill. Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions.

fields.name: aurastatcalc#
fields.description: Calculation Field. Controls the value for the relative aurastat# field.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: auraevent#
fields.description: Controls what event will trigger the relative auraeventfunc# field function. Used as a possible parameter used by various skill functions.

fields.name: auraeventfunc#
fields.description: Controls the function used when the relative auraevent# event is triggered. Corresponds to a Server Event Functions (enums).

fields.name: passivestate
fields.description: Links to a state that is automatically applied as a passive when the skill gains levels.

fields.name: passiveitype
fields.description: Links to an Item Type to define what type of item needs to be equipped in order to enable the passivestate. Not all stats support this behavior, usually only ones with "mastery" in the name.

fields.name: passivereqweaponcount
fields.description: Controls how many equipped weapons are needed for the passivestate to be enabled. If the value equals 1, then the player must have 1 weapon equipped for the passivestate to be enabled. If the value equals 2, then the player must be dual wielding weapons for the passivestate to be enabled. If the value equals 0, then ignore this field. Not all stats support this behavior, usually only ones with "mastery" in the name.

fields.name: passivestat#
fields.description: Assigns stat modifiers to the passivestate.

fields.name: passivecalc#
fields.description: Calculation Field. Controls the value for the relative passivestat# field.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: summon
fields.description: Controls what monster is summoned by the skill. This field's usage will depend on the skill function used. This field can also be used as reference for AI behaviors and for the skilldesc.txt file.

fields.name: pettype
fields.description: Links to a pet type data to control how the summoned unit is displayed on the UI

fields.name: petmax
fields.description: Calculation Field. Used skill functions that summon pets to control how many summon units are allowed at a time.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: requirespettype
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the skill requires at least one pet of the pettype.txt to cast.

fields.name: summode
fields.description: Defines the animation mode that the summoned monster will be initiated with. Uses a code (MonMode).

fields.name: sumskill#
fields.description: Assigns a skill to the summoned monster. This can be useful for adding a skill to a monster to transition its synergy bonuses.

fields.name: sumsk#calc
fields.description: Calculation Field. Controls the skill level for the designated sumskill# field when the skill is assigned to the monster.
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: sumumod
fields.description: Assigns a monster modifier to the summoned monster. Uses the index of an entry in monumod.txt
fields.format: Skill scope BBE. See BBE/Calc Fields

fields.name: sumoverlay
fields.description: Creates an overlay on the summoned monster when it is first created.

fields.name: stsuccessonly
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then the following sound and overlay fields will only play when the skill is successfully cast, instead of always being used even when the skill cast is interrupted. If equals 0, then the following sound and overlay fields will always be used when the skill is cast, regardless if the skill was interrupted or not.

fields.name: stsound
fields.description: Controls what client sound is played when the skill is used, based on the client starting function

fields.name: stsoundclass
fields.description: Controls what client sound is played when the skill is used by the skill's assigned class (See charclass field), based on the client starting function. If the unit using the skill is not the same class as the charclass value for the skill, then this sound will not play.

fields.name: stsounddelay
fields.description: Boolean Field. If equals 1, then use the weapon's hit class to determine the delay in frames (where 25 frames = 1 second) before playing the skill's start sound. If equals 0, then the skill's start sound will play immediately.

fields.name: weaponsnd

Also use the sound delay based on the weapon's hit class to determine the delay in frames (where 25 frames = 1 second) before playing the weapon hit sound (See stsounddelay for the types of hit class sounds and delays used). If equals 0, then do not play the weapon hit sound when hitting an enemy with the skill attack.
